title.narrative: Cross border initiative to strengthen resilience, community-based protection and conflict prevention capacities for peace in the fragile border region of Côte d’Ivoire and Liberia.

description.narrative: Following almost 15 years of civil war, Liberia was left with its economic, social, and political structures and its infrastructure decimated. The country has been in the process of rebuilding; but this process has been concentrated in the capital and rural regions have yet to feel its effects. Liberia suffers from widespread poverty and underdevelopment, with worrisome indicators in income, poverty, education, health, good governance, water and sanitation, and equality; in 2013 Liberia ranked 174 / 186 on UNDPs Human Development Index; Côte d'Ivoire- still suffering from massive social schisms along ethnic lines- ranked 168.Gender inequality and women's marginalisation are entrenched in both coutries. Sexual abuse, physical abuse, neglect, and child labour are common. Child labour in Liberia is estimated at 21%, and in Côte d'Ivoire 35% of school-aged children work. Although, education is the route to development, the majority of Liberian children still reach puberty illiterate, having started school late, repeated classes year after year, and failed to achieve meaningful learning outcomes. In Côte d'Ivoire, statistics show significant differences in the enrollment rates for boys and girls in school, with the gap increasing as children get older. The population on both sides of the border continues to rely upon traditional power and decision-making structures; due in part to the absence of qualified, capacitated and trusted State actors with the ability to intervene when problems arise. This action is an extension of the current ECHO funded CROSS-BORDER PROGRAMME and will capitalise on the joint framework already established. DRC will focus on strengthening community-based protection mechanisms; capacity-building for State actors; the promotion of social cohesion; and strengthened livelihood opportunities, including agricultural activities, for vulnerable groups.
